signals.title: NOK/EUR — G10 Bilateral Theme + Crude Disruption
signals.text: NOK leads G10 performance with a 1W average gain of +0.862% across 2 pairs, while EUR anchors the laggard board at -0.556% across 9 pairs, driving a 1.418% bilateral spread. Maritime disruptions following unverified explosions in the Strait of Hormuz and US crude sanctions push WTI up +3.70% to $91.5, underpinning the petro-currency. Norges Bank policy rate at 4.5% versus ECB at 2.65% maintains a 185bp nominal rate advantage in NOK's favor, while real rate spreads stand at +1.82% for NOK versus +0.30% for EUR. EUR/NOK spot at 10.7161 screens cheap on BEER fair-value modeling at z = -2.48σ, while retail positioning shows a 100% extreme short exposure. Trade bias: Bullish NOK/EUR; crude supply shock and 185bp policy rate divergence reinforce the trend. Catalyst: ECB Schnabel speech tomorrow at 13:30 UTC. Risk: Strait of Hormuz transit normalizes rapidly, driving WTI below $85 and compressing the bilateral spread under 0.80%.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Fed Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY prints at 157.84, positioned above its SMA20 at 156.87 and SMA50 at 157.69 but contained below the 200-day moving average at 158.51. Spot holds below 160.00, the threshold where Ministry of Finance verbal warnings and intervention sensitivity historically intensify. Saxo 1M 25d risk reversals display a sharp downside put skew of -1.82 against an options implied volatility of 8.0% versus HV30 of 9.9%, yielding an inverted vol risk premium of -1.9%. The OIS carry spread between SOFR at 3.90% and TONA at 1.23% sustains a +267bp carry buffer in the greenback's favor, yet MOVE sits at the 94th percentile of its trailing year while VIX rests at the 22nd percentile, signaling elevated rates volatility that equity markets have yet to register. CFTC speculative positioning reveals leveraged funds net short JPY by -16,809 contracts, sitting at the 96th percentile of its 52-week historical range with a z-score of +1.83. Trade bias: Neutral/consolidative USD/JPY, capped near the 200-day moving average as strong options put skew hedges carry exposure. Catalyst: Japan Household Spending data tonight at 23:30 UTC. Risk: A daily close above the 200-day moving average at 158.51 triggers momentum buying toward 160.00.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Speculative Short + Elevated Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1211, suppressed beneath its entire moving average stack including the SMA20 at 1.1404, SMA50 at 1.1519, and SMA200 at 1.1605. Saxo 1M implied volatility runs at 6.7% against 30-day realized volatility of 4.2%, establishing an elevated vol risk premium of +2.6%. CFTC data for the week ending September 29 shows leveraged funds net short -82,445 contracts, positioned in the 6th percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of -1.65 following a WoW reduction of -23,640 contracts. OIS benchmarks show SOFR at 3.90% against €STR at 2.44%, locking in a +146bp carry advantage favoring the dollar. US 5Y yields stand at 5.06%, up +52bp over 20 sessions led by real yields adding +53bp while breakevens shifted -1bp. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; carry disadvantage and structural moving-average overhead keep spot defensive. Catalyst: ECB Schnabel speech tomorrow at 13:30 UTC. Risk: Speculative short covering pushes spot through the SMA20 at 1.1404.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Technical Resistance + Positive Carry Cushion
signals.text: AUD/USD prints at 0.6957, holding below its downward-sloping SMA200 at 0.7037, SMA20 at 0.7052, and SMA50 at 0.7094. The currency pair retains positive carry as RBA AONIA at 4.60% trades 70bp above US SOFR at 3.90%, offering structural support against broader US dollar firmness. Leveraged funds maintain net long exposure of +55,114 contracts at the 79th percentile of the 52-week distribution, while 1M 25d risk reversals post a moderate put skew of -0.99. Australia's 10Y sovereign yield trades at 5.40%, holding a +9bp premium over the US 10Y at 5.31%, while 2Y spreads favor AUD by +13bp. Trade bias: Neutral/range AUD/USD; 70bp positive carry cushion offsets moving average resistance overhead. Catalyst: next RBA meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on 3 Nov with cash rate on hold. Risk: Daily settlement above the SMA200 at 0.7037 invalidates technical overhead and opens a test of the 0.7100 handle.
